p: Next, a contact sheet: ONE square image divided into a 2 x 2 grid of four equal square panels with thin plain gaps between them. Each panel is a separate studio product photo in exactly the master style (same warm grey backdrop, same lighting, same three-quarter front-left angle, object filling about 80% of its panel, matte black finish unless stated, unbranded, no text, no people). Top left: A cambered bar, a long Olympic-length barbell whose centre section bends downwards in a pronounced drop on each side so the loaded sleeves hang below shoulder height, or a gently curved bow bar version. Top right: An axle / fat bar, a thick un-knurled steel bar about 50 mm in diameter with no rotating sleeves, the whole bar the same thickness end to end, loaded with plates near each end. Bottom left: A set of fixed-weight barbells, a row of short barbells with plates permanently welded at each end, each one with a numbered weight on the end cap, resting horizontally on a tiered upright rack. Bottom right: A landmine, a heavy steel floor base or rack-mounted post with a rotating sleeve that pivots in all directions, holding one end of a barbell that rises at an angle with a single plate loaded on the far end.

Next, a contact sheet: ONE square image divided into a 2 x 2 grid of four equal square panels with thin plain gaps between them. Each panel is a separate studio product photo in exactly the master style (same warm grey backdrop, same lighting, same three-quarter front-left angle, object filling about 80% of its panel, matte black finish unless stated, unbranded, no text, no people). Top left: A Smith machine, a tall steel frame with a barbell fixed to vertical guide rods so it runs straight up and down, with hooks on the bar that rotate into slots on the uprights, plate pegs on the bar and adjustable safety stops at the base. Top right: An angled Smith machine, a Smith machine whose twin guide rods lean backwards at a slight angle of about 7 degrees, with a counterweighted barbell on the rails, rotating hooks and plate pegs, and safety stops at the base. Bottom left: A 3D Smith machine, a large Smith machine whose barbell rides on a carriage that slides both up and down and forwards and backwards on horizontal rails across the top of the frame, allowing movement in two planes. Bottom right: A decline bench, a padded bench angled head-down at about 20 degrees with a padded leg hook roller at the raised end to lock the legs in and a small pair of bar uprights at the low end.

Top left: A set of spotter / safety arms, a pair of long steel safety arms with a rubber-lined top surface pinned to the uprights of a rack, alongside a pair of J-shaped bar hooks. Top right: A bench leg extension / curl attachment, a pivoting steel arm attached to the front of a weight bench, with two pairs of foam rollers for the shins and a loading horn for plates at the end of the arm. Bottom left: A set of rack lever arms, a pair of long steel lever arms that pin into the lower holes of a power rack upright at each side and pivot upwards, each with a handle near the free end and a short loading sleeve for plates. Bottom right: A set of adjustable dumbbells, a pair of adjustable dumbbells sitting in their moulded cradles, each with a handle inside a stack of nested weight plates and a selector dial or pin to choose the load.

Top left: A cable crossover (two stacks), a wide steel frame with two separate weight stack towers on either side joined by a crossbar with a pull-up bar, each tower with a pulley that slides up and down a vertical rail. Top right: A functional trainer, a compact steel frame with two weight stacks side by side and a pair of swinging pulley arms that slide up and down vertical columns on each side, with multi-grip pull-up handles on the top crossbar. Bottom left: A lat pulldown, an upright frame with a seat and padded thigh roller pads in front of a weight stack, a high pulley above the seat holding a long wide bar with angled ends. Bottom right: A lat pulldown / low row combo, a single weight stack machine with a seat and thigh pads under a high pulley holding a lat bar, plus a low pulley and footplate at the front for seated rows.

Top left: A plate-loaded pulley (DIY), a single steel pulley clamped to the top crossmember of a rack, with a steel cable running over it down to a vertical loading pin with plates at the bottom and a handle at the other end. Top right: A multi-station cable jungle, a large central steel frame with four weight stacks arranged around it, each feeding a different station: a lat pulldown seat, a low row bench, a high and low adjustable pulley and a crossover arm. Bottom left: An ab crunch machine, a pin-loaded machine with a seat, padded foot rollers and padded handles or chest pads on an arm above, which curl down towards the knees, and a weight stack at the side. Bottom right: A rotary torso, a pin-loaded machine with a rotating seat, padded knee and chest pads and handles, which twists from side to side, with a weight stack at the rear.
